annotations.title: Start an X AI Assistant Chat Job

description: Starts the same Grok chat as the buffered Grok chat call without holding the connection open, for clients that stop waiting before a search-grounded answer arrives. Takes the same arguments and returns 202 at once with job_id, status 'pending', poll (the path to read the job at), poll_after_seconds (3), result_ttl_seconds (900) and created_at. A bad body, a bad API key, a missing X session and a short balance are answered on the spot, before any job exists. At most 5 jobs per API key can be pending at once; one more answers 429 too_many_pending_jobs. Submitting is free: the $0.004 Grok chat price is charged once, on the poll that first delivers the finished answer, and a failed, timed-out, interrupted or uncollected job is not charged. Requires an authenticated X session for the acting account, and the chat runs as that account. Cost: Free per call. Docs: https://docs.twitterapis.com/docs/reference/grok/grok-chat-submit

auth_token.description: Optional. The account's auth_token cookie; together with ct0, this call acts as that account. Sent out of band: as the x-auth-token request header on most endpoints, or inside the JSON request body on endpoints that take one. It is not sent as a query parameter, so it does not reach a URL or an access log.

conversation_id.description: Conversation id returned by a previous call. Absent on the first turn, in which case a new conversation is opened and its id returned.

ct0.description: Optional. The account's ct0 cookie, paired with auth_token. Same transport as auth_token: the x-ct0 request header, or the JSON body on a body-taking endpoint. It is not sent as a query parameter.

image_count.description: Forwarded to X as its image-generation count, clamped to 0 through 4 (default 4, the value X's own client sends); 0 asks for a text-only answer. The reply has no image field, so a generated image is not returned.

message.description: The prompt, for a single-turn question, up to 20,000 characters. A bare tweet or status URL is a first-class input and comes back as a summary of that post. Either this or messages[] is required.

messages.description: Prior turns for a multi-turn conversation, oldest first, as an array of { role: 'user' | 'assistant', content: '...' } objects, up to 100 (X's own { sender: 1 | 2, message } shape also works, 2 being Grok). The endpoint stores nothing, so this array is the whole history Grok sees. Either this or message is required; without message, the last entry is the prompt, and it needs to be a user turn.

mode.description: Which Grok answers: 'auto' (default, balanced), 'fast' (quicker, less thorough) or 'expert' (slowest, most thorough). The response reports which model actually answered, which can differ from the mode requested.

proxy_url.description: Optional. Residential proxy URL this call egresses through. X soft-blocks writes from datacenter IPs as automated. Honoured on write endpoints on its own; on a read endpoint it is honoured only when auth_token and ct0 are sent with it, otherwise the read leaves through the session's own egress. Sent as the x-proxy-url request header, or in the JSON body on a body-taking endpoint.

user_agent.description: Optional. User-Agent string sent for this session. Sent as the x-user-agent request header, or in the JSON body on a body-taking endpoint.
